newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Yankee cleanup cost seen at $100mln.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Yankee cleanup cost seen at $100mln.

text.p: The cleanup costs of contaminated grounds around the closed Connecticut Yankee nuclear power station could exceed $100 million, the Hartford Courant reported Thursday.
The report cited internal documents of Northeast Utilities, and said some 212,000 cubic feet of pavement and soil may be riddled with radioactive contamination.
Northeast Utilities spokespersons were not immediately available for comment.
The utility has stated publically that it expects to pay $12.6 million to clean up 93,000 cubic feet of grounds contaminated by leaks and spills during the plant's 30 years of operation.
The 582-megawatt Connecticut Yankee plant in Haddam Neck, Conn., was operated and 49-percent-owned by Northeast Utilities, with the balance owned by seven other New England utilities.
It was shut down in July 1996 for safety reasons, and permanently closed last December.
Northeast has estimated that the plant's decommissioning will cost more than $420 million.
The Courant quoted Northeast officials who conceded that they do not know the extent to which radiation has found its way into the soil and pavement around the plant.

The report said surveys conducted by Connecticut Yankee radiation officers last year found that "significant amounts of radioactivity" remain in the ground around and beneath a nearby basketball court -- possibly down to a depth of five feet.

Northeast's three Millstone nuclear power plants in Waterford, Conn., with combined capacity of 2,700 MW, have been closed for safety reasons since March 1996. The utility hopes to bring them back on line by early 1998.
